newsitem.title: CANADA: Montrealers still owe plenty for 1976 Olympic stadium.
newsitem.headline: Montrealers still owe plenty for 1976 Olympic stadium.

text.p: Montreal taxpayers still owe C$435 million on the stadium built for the 1976 Summer Olympics in Montreal, the Quebec minister responsible for the metropolis said (on) Wednesday.
When taxpayers in Montreal and the rest of the French-speaking province finish paying a special levy for the stadium in 2006, it will have cost a total of C$1.4 billion, said Serge Menard.

Menard made his comments after the board that manages the stadium announced it had hired U.S. engineering firm Bird Air to build a new non-retractable fiberglass roof for the facility at a cost of C$37 million. If approved by the Quebec cabinet, construction would begin in mid-June.

The current roof was installed in 1987, but its space-age kevlar fabric was damaged by lying in storage for many years, and it could not be retracted as originally planned by French architect Roger Taillibert.

The landmark, avant-garde stadium often has been criticized as a monument to public sector folly and construction sector corruption. Even with a new roof, it may have trouble keeping its main tenant, the Montreal Expos National League baseball franchise.

Long suffering from low fan attendance in the cavernous stadium despite fielding a perennially competitive team, the Expos are trying to generate support for building a smaller, open-air stadium steps from the city core.
